newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt says it wants Palestinians to sign agreement.
newsitem.headline: Egypt says it wants Palestinians to sign agreement.

text.p: Egypt said on Tuesday that because it wanted peace it would never try to stop the Palestinians from signing an agreement with Israel.
President Hosni Mubarak was answering a chronic Israeli complaint that surfaced again last week in an interview the Israeli ambassador in Washington gave to the Washington Times.
"If they (the Israelis) accuse us of this, we will accuse them that they did not implement what was agreed upon and signed in Washington and Cairo," Mubarak told a news conference.
"We will never persuade the Palestinians to delay any signature or agreement, because we are keen on peace, but fair peace," the president added.
"We don't want this to make any complication in relations between the two countries (Egypt and Israel)," he said.

Israeli ambassador Eliahu Ben-Elissar, asked if Egypt was encouraging Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat to slow down or block agreement on a withdrawal of Israeli troops from Hebron, said, "Yes. Unfortunately, the Eygptians have not been enthusiastic during this process for their own reasons."

Mubarak, who has refused to see Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu until Israel and the Palestinians agree on Hebron, said the prospects were now better that Middle East peace talks could progress.
Egypt and Jordan stepped in on Sunday with a compromise on the deadline for Israel to complete other redeployments after Hebron. The date is now expected to be mid-1998.
"I am very optimistic that the process will move ahead," Mubarak said. "Mr Netanyahu is not alone in taking the decision. He has his cabinet and he is meeting some problems in his cabinet," he added.
"Let us put an end to problems and terrorism and everything that's happening in this part of the world," he said.
Mubarak, who has been in close contact with the main parties to the Hebron talks, concurred with reports that an agreement was imminent, either on Tuesday or Wednesday.
